name: LZ77 sliding-window backreference
definition: For input x[0..n−1], window W≥1, maximum length L≥2 and position i, define ℓ(d)=max{k: 0≤k≤min(L,n−i), x[i+j]=x[i+j−d] for all 0≤j<k}, for 1≤d≤min(W,i). Choose maximum ℓ(d), breaking ties by smallest d. If a match of length at least 2 exists, emit tagged pair (d,ℓ) and advance i by ℓ; otherwise emit tagged literal x[i] and advance by one. Decoder appends y[|y|−d] repeatedly ℓ times, recalculating the current output length each time.
variables: x input, n length, i current position, W window bound, L length bound, d distance, ℓ match length, y decoded prefix
assumptions: Finite equality-comparable symbols; fixed shared integer W and L; empty initial dictionary; framed tagged tokens and exact expected output length; overlapping references permitted; empty input encodes as no tokens
limitations: Direct exhaustive matching takes O(nWL) symbol comparisons as a conservative bound; decoding takes O(n) symbol writes with O(W) history beyond output. Greedy longest matching is not necessarily bit-optimal; this specifies a simplified token parser, not original triple framing or the full DEFLATE format
failure_conditions: Invalid window or length bounds, unknown tag or invalid literal
Reference distance outside 1..min(W,decoded length), length outside 2..L, truncated token
Decoded output exceeds declared length or resource limit, or final length differs
computation: Enumerate admissible distances in ascending order and extend each match until mismatch or limit; emit longest eligible match or a literal. Validate bounds and expected remaining output before decoding each token; overlap uses forward symbol-by-symbol copying rather than a static slice.

source.citation: Deutsch (1996), RFC 1951, DEFLATE Compressed Data Format Specification, §§2 and 3.2.3, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1951.html (literal and distance/length token model, overlapping copies; this specification generalizes bounds and uses its own greedy rule and framing). Ziv and Lempel (1977), A Universal Algorithm for Sequential Data Compression, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 23(3), 337–343, DOI 10.1109/TIT.1977.1055714 (metadata and abstract reviewed; original full paper not reviewed).

application: General lossless sequence representation; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite symbol sequence or tagged token stream, shared W and L, declared output length and resource cap.
incompatible_methods: Static non-overlapping slice decoding for overlapping matches
Assuming greedy parsing is bit-optimal or claiming DEFLATE compatibility
mechanism_note: Each copied symbol references an already produced symbol because d≥1, including within overlapping copies; induction on decoded length proves lossless reconstruction. Unlike LZ78, no persistent phrase dictionary or phrase-index insertion is required; references are bounded relative positions. This is a distinct sliding-window mechanism.

name: Run-length encoding symbol-count pairs
definition: For a finite sequence x of length n, partition into maximal equal-symbol runs (s_i,c_i), c_i≥1, adjacent s_i≠s_(i+1), and Σ_i c_i=n. Encode the ordered pairs; decode x=s_1 repeated c_1 times followed by subsequent runs in order. Empty input has zero pairs.
variables: s_i run symbol, c_i positive run length, n input length, r number of maximal runs
assumptions: Finite equality-comparable symbols with unambiguous representation; framed pairs and declared output length; exact bounded positive integer counts; adjacent equal-symbol pairs rejected under this canonical unsplit-run convention
limitations: Encoding and decoding require O(n) symbol operations and O(1) working words beyond input/output in a bounded-count word model; r≤n for nonempty input. Actual encoded size depends on count and symbol representation, and may expand; fixed-width split-run formats and PackBits are not specified
failure_conditions: Nonpositive or noninteger count, unknown symbol or malformed pair
Adjacent pairs with equal symbols under canonical framing
Sum of counts exceeds declared output size or resource limit, or final sum differs
computation: Scan the input once, accumulating a count for the current symbol and flushing on change or end. Validate the complete pair framing, counts, adjacency and cumulative length before expansion; then emit the declared number of each symbol.

source.citation: Kulcu, Algorithms Lecture Notes, Chapter 9: String Matching and Compression, §9.8.1, https://sercankulcu.github.io/files/algorithms/notes/Chapter_09_String_Matching_and_Compression_Lecture_Notes.html (maximal runs and count-symbol pairs). TIFF Image File Format Rev. 4.0, Appendix C, https://cool.culturalheritage.org/bytopic/imaging/std/tiff4.html (historical PackBits repeat packets; not the same wire format).

application: General lossless sequence representation; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite symbol sequence or framed symbol/count pairs, declared output length and resource cap.
incompatible_methods: Treating a global symbol histogram as contiguous runs
Assuming fixed-width counts without overflow handling or guaranteed compression
mechanism_note: Run boundaries occur exactly at unequal adjacent symbols; the unique maximal-run partition is recovered from its ordered symbols and lengths. This is not Golomb coding of integers, nor general LZ77 substring substitution; although long constant runs can be represented using distance-one LZ77 references, the canonical run partition is a different sequence representation.
